correctness.rationale: Fraïssé homogeneity reduces complete types to all finite labelled strict poset extensions of the fixed chain. Every new point has a unique pair 0<=ell_i<=u_i<=n of predecessor/successor cut positions. The necessary relation inequalities for comparable and incomparable tuple points are exactly the isotonicity arrows of Q_F. Conversely the proof checks all mixed triples and forces any x_i<a_t<x_j comparison to agree with F; no extra transitive closure constraints remain. Thus T_r(n)=sum_F Ω_QF(n+1). Surjective isotone images of sizes k=1..2r yield strictly positive integer c_r,k because any linear extension can be coalesced into k nonempty consecutive blocks, establishing degree precisely 2r. Independently direct full ternary-relation closure matches endpoint formula in 12 configurations. The closed r<=3 formulas have been checked against original verifier and structural constraints.

value.rationale: Parameter-dependent complete type spectra are natural invariants of the countable generic poset. The explicit arity-uniform endpoint representation, sharp degree 2r, strict positivity of all binomial-coefficient layers, and limiting 1/4:1/4:1/2 relation split are useful structural facts, not merely a finite sequence lookup. This contrasts polynomial growth over chain parameters with established exponential growth over antichains.
residual_risks: Computation of coefficient lists for unbounded r may be expensive; no practical complexity claim.

final_claim: For every tuple arity r>=1, the number of injective labelled complete r-types over an n-point individually named chain in the countable homogeneous random poset is the sum of order polynomials of explicit 2r-element endpoint posets, has exact degree 2r, and has positive integer binomial-spectrum coefficients.
limitations: The original numerical n=0 labelled-poset counts and r=2 quartic are known; random-poset r=1 chain count covered explicitly by published Resultary prior.
No uniform algorithmic precomputation bound in growing arity.
An unlocated all-arity exact type count could dominate the new result.
